title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (§44 of the 'Longue Marche' sequel, Grothendieck's manuscript p. 356): π̂ = π̂_{0,3} is the profinite fundamental group of P^1 minus {0,1,∞}, a free profinite group of rank 2. Γ̂^+_{0,3} is its extension by the 'modular' quotient C^+_{0,3} = S_3, presented by σ_∞^2 = ρ^3 = 1. The object of study is an automorphism u of Γ̂^+_{0,3} that induces the identity on S_3; up to the stated caveats this is the same as an automorphism of π̂_{0,3}. Such a u is determined by u(σ_∞) = hσ_∞ and u(ρ) = gρ with g, h in π̂, subject to the conditions hσ_∞(h) = 1 and gρ(g)ρ^2(g) = 1 from the previous page.

On this page Grothendieck reinterprets g and h. Let u act on Aut(π̂), with ρ and σ_∞ acting on π̂ by conjugation. Then u∘int(ρ)∘u^{-1} = int(u(ρ)) = int(g)∘int(ρ). So the commutator [u,ρ] = uρu^{-1}ρ^{-1} equals int(g), and likewise [u,σ_∞] = int(h); this is formula (4). Because π̂ is centre-free, g and h are determined by these inner automorphisms. Conversely, g and h determine u, since σ_∞ and ρ generate Γ̂^+_{0,3}. Grothendieck calls this 'remarkable'.

He then imposes compatibility of u with the 'structure of loops' (inertia preservation). For each of the three punctures i ∈ {0,1,∞} he requires u(l_i) = int(g_i)·l_i^p, with a single multiplier p ∈ Ẑ^× and conjugators g_i ∈ π̂. He notes that the name g_0 is unfortunate because it clashes with g, whose role is quite different. On the next page he renames things: g_0 becomes f_0^{-1} and p becomes μ, giving the 'relation de lacets' u(ε_0) = int(f_0^{-1})ε_0^μ.

In modern terms this is the passage to the description of GT-type automorphisms of F̂_2 by a pair (λ, f): σ(x) = x^λ, σ(y) = f^{-1}y^λ f. Conditions (2) are the S_3-symmetric analogues of Drinfeld's 2-cycle relation (order-2 symmetry σ_∞) and 3-cycle/hexagon relation (order-3 symmetry ρ). The page thus serves the 'mise en équations' of the outer action of Gal(Q̄/Q) on the tower of Teichmüller groups, starting at level (0,3).
errors: No mathematical error. Two minor points of precision. (i) Formula (4) treats ρ and σ_∞ as inner automorphisms of π̂ (via conjugation inside Γ̂^+), so the commutator lives in Aut(π̂); reading off g and h from int(g) and int(h) uses that π̂_{0,3} is centre-free, which is true but not stated. (ii) 'σ_∞, ρ engendrent' must refer to Γ̂^+_{0,3}, not a symmetric group; the transcription's 𝔖^+_{0,3} is a misreading.

ideas.what: Coding an automorphism u of Γ̂^+_{0,3} = π̂_{0,3}·S_3 by the pair (g,h) with u(ρ) = gρ, u(σ_∞) = hσ_∞, interpreted as commutators [u,ρ] = int(g), [u,σ_∞] = int(h).
ideas.modern_name: Cocycle/commutator description of automorphisms of F̂_2 ⋊ S_3; the order-2 and order-3 relations of the Grothendieck–Teichmüller group
ideas.usually_credited_to: Drinfeld (1990) for GT; Ihara, Lochak–Schneps for the profinite version
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme only sketches the idea of GT acting on the Teichmüller tower; these explicit equations appear in the unpublished Longue Marche material

ideas.what: Loop (inertia) compatibility u(l_i) = int(g_i) l_i^p for the three punctures, with a common multiplier p ∈ Ẑ^×.
ideas.modern_name: Inertia-preserving (braid-like) automorphisms; the (λ,f) parametrisation of GT̂
ideas.where_published: Longue Marche à travers la théorie de Galois (1981, circulated partially); Esquisse d'un programme mentions the loop condition qualitatively

missed.claim: This is pre-Drinfeld documentary evidence that Grothendieck set up GT-type equations in an S_3-symmetric form. The order-2 condition hσ_∞(h) = 1 and order-3 condition gρ(g)ρ²(g) = 1 come together with the inertia ('lacets') condition carrying a multiplier μ ∈ Ẑ^× and a conjugator f_0, matching Drinfeld's (λ,f). The historical fact is broadly known; the explicit notation-level details are not widely documented.
missed.quote: c'est une chose remarquable que la connaissance des éléments g, h de π qui vérifient (4), implique déjà la connaissance de u
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Relevant for the history of GT. The symmetric (ρ, σ_∞) presentation is close to the 'S_3-equivariant' presentations of GT used later; no new mathematics beyond that.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a clean pre-Drinfeld formulation of the level-(0,3) equations defining what became GT̂, including the loop condition with a multiplier. That Grothendieck had this is known in outline to specialists, and the content itself is routine.
transcription_corrections: First line: the words after 'les éléments g et h,' are not reliably read as transcribed (likely 'pris dans un des ... de π̂_{0,3}'); the phrase is uncertain.
'grâce au fait que σ_∞, ρ engendrent Γ̂^+_{0,3}' — the transcription's 𝔖^+_{0,3} should be Γ̂^+_{0,3}.
'L'indice 0 dans g_0 était destiné à permettre ici, plus généralement' — 'prévoir' is probably 'permettre'.
In (4) the underbrace under uρu^{-1} reads u(ρ), as transcribed.
'l_0' is probably ℓ_0 (loop), parallel to ε_0.
